blocks.text: מַעֲרִיב לֵיל שֵׁנִי שֶׁל ראשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר בִּדְבָרוֹ מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים בְּחָכְמָה פֹּתֵחַ שְׁעָרִים וּבִתְבוּנָה מְשַׁנֶּה עִתִּים וּמַחֲלִיף אֶת־הַזְּמַנִּים וּמְסַדֵּר אֶת־הַכֹּכָבִים בְּמִשְׁמְרֹתֵיהֶם בָּרָקִיעַ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ בּוֹרֵא יוֹם וָלָֽיְלָה גּוֹלֵל אוֹר מִפְּנֵי־חֹשֶׁךְ וְחֹשֶׁךְ מִפְּנֵי־אוֹר. וּמַעֲבִיר יוֹם וּמֵבִיא לָֽיְלָה וּמַבְדִּיל בֵּין יוֹם וּבֵין לָֽיְלָה יְיָ צְבָאוֹת שְׁמוֹ. אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם תָּמִיד יִמְלוֹךְ עָלֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמַּעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים:

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרוֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא רִאשׁוֹן וְהוּא אַחֲרוֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדָיו אֵין אֱלֹהִים סֹלּוּ לָרֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ וְעִלְזוּ לְפָנָיו. וּשְׁמוֹ מְרוֹמָם עַל־כָּל־בְּרָכָה וּתְהִלָּה:
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד:
יְהִי שֵׁם יְיָ מְבֹרָךְ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם:

אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ אָהָבְתָּ, תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ, עַל־כֵּן יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּשָׁכְבֵנוּ וּבְקוּמֵנוּ נָשִׂיחַ בְּחֻקֶּיךָ, וְנִשְׂמַח בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ וּבְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד, כִּי הֵם חַיֵּינוּ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֵינוּ וּבָהֶם נֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָֽיְלָה. וְאַהֲבָתְךָ אַל־תָּסִיר מִמֶּנּוּ לְעוֹלָמִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אוֹהֵב עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל:
שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה ׀ אֶחָד:
בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֔ אֵת יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁךָ וּבְכָל־מְאֹדֶֽךָ: וְהָי֞וּ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם עַל־

The page is laid out as follows. The heading runs between the page numbers 2 and 2. Under it are two columns: the right column is headed פֿאָרבעטער (reader) and the left column is headed געמיינדע (congregation). The reader's text starts in the right column and runs on at full width from הַזְּמַנִּים. In שְׁמַע the ע is enlarged, and so is the ד in אֶחָד. The page ends in the middle of a verse at עַל־.

uncertainties.question: I can't tell if a holam is printed over the resh or alef, or if the word is written without it.
These Yiddish/German role labels are printed small. I can't fully confirm the rafe on פֿ, the qamats under א, or the exact letter sequence ייגד versus יינד.
The small label under בָּרְכוּ looks like קה״ח or קה״ל. I read it as קה״ל (קהל, the congregation), but the last letter isn't clear.
I can't tell whether the word is defective (holam on the resh) or written with a full vav.
There is a meteg-like mark next to the qamats under the lamed. I'm not sure it is a meteg each time it appears. On יָמֵינוּ I can't tell whether there is one at all.
I can't confirm the hiriq under the resh.
I can't confirm that the holam and the dagesh in the lamed are present.
This looks defective (no vav), which would differ from לְעוֹלָם elsewhere on the page. I'm not sure.
This is small Rashi script and could also be read as יסיד אומר. I read it as יחיד.
This small Rashi citation could read דברים ו ד. I'm not sure whether there are geresh marks or only spacing.

uncertainties.word: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה אֶחָד
uncertainties.question: There are small marks under and over these words that may be cantillation, for example under the alef of יִשְׂרָאֵל, under אֱלֹהֵינוּ, and under the vav of each יְהוָה. At this resolution I can't tell accents apart from vowel points, so I've left accents out of this verse. The small vertical mark between יְהוָה and אֶחָד looks like a paseq (׀), but it could also be a small yod-like ornament.
I can't confirm a silluq under the dalet. The sof pasuq is printed as a diamond-shaped colon.
This is small Rashi script before בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם. I'm fairly confident in the reading.
A zaqef qatan seems to be over the tav, and there is a mark under the alef that could be a meteg or a munach. I'm not sure of either.

uncertainties.question: There are faint marks here that are probably accents (tipcha, munach, atnach, merkha, silluq). I can't identify any of them for certain, so I left them out. Only the mark under מְאֹדֶֽךָ is recorded, as a possible silluq or meteg.
A double mark over the yod looks like gershayim. I'm moderately confident.

uncertainties.question: Each of these words has accent-like marks above or below it (possibly munach, revia, telisha, darga, tevir, tipcha). I can't settle them at this resolution, so I left them out of the text.

completeness_limitations: I read every word on the page. Vowel points are given as I could see them. Cantillation is fully recorded only where it was legible: the zaqef on וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֔ and the gershayim on וְהָי֞וּ, plus possible meteg and silluq marks. All other accent marks in the Shema and in the first verse of וְאָהַבְתָּ are left out of the text and listed as uncertainties, because the scan resolution doesn't let me tell them apart from vowels or name them. The small Rashi labels are read with moderate confidence. The page ends in the middle of a verse at עַל־.
